correctness.rationale: For Haar-normalized SU(2), the Weyl constant-term identity gives exact moments through order six for every integer n>=2. Positivity of tensor multiplicities reduces all complex phases to the aligned case. For odd n the normalized moment is a strict Bernstein-control-value convex combination with unique maximum S_n at the pure character. For even n the derivative numerator H_n has H_n(0)>0 and strictly negative nonconstant coefficients, hence exactly one positive zero, a unique global maximum and strict gain. Uniform expansion near x=5/(4n) proves the advertised O(n^-2) optimizer and 75n/32+O(1) gain. The standalone independent-formula checker passed 983 finite assertions; infinite assertions follow analytically, not from these tests.
